evals.name: show-names-the-supplying-layer
evals.expected_output: The effective configuration with the layer supplying each value, read from the detectors' own --show-config output rather than by parsing the JSON files by hand. When no layer exists, it reports the bundled defaults as the effective values rather than reporting an error.
expectations: Runs list-corpus.sh --show-config and check-stamps.sh --show-config rather than reading the config files directly
Names which of the three layers supplies each effective value
Treats all three layers absent as a valid state that yields the bundled defaults, not as an error
Does not write any file for a show action

evals.name: set-one-key-preserves-the-rest
evals.prompt: /attribution:setup set stamp_expiry_days 90 in a repository whose team config already sets excluded_paths and a corpus_fetch_ceiling.
evals.expected_output: Only stamp_expiry_days changes in the team layer. excluded_paths and budgets.corpus_fetch_ceiling are preserved byte-for-byte. The write is a per-key edit, never a regenerated file that restates the whole schema.
expectations: Changes only the named key and leaves every other existing key intact
Does NOT rewrite the file from the full default schema, which would turn unmentioned keys into accidental decisions
Writes to the team layer by default, and to the local overlay only when the user asked for it
Reports the resulting effective value and the layer it now comes from

evals.name: rejects-a-key-outside-the-schema
evals.expected_output: The write is refused with the reason: judge_samples is a top-level key, and an accuracy.judge_samples entry would be a silent no-op that quietly halves the panel while reading like a setting. The correct form, setting the top-level judge_samples, is offered.
expectations: Refuses to write accuracy.judge_samples rather than accepting it
States that the misplaced key would be a silent no-op, not merely that it is unrecognized
Offers the correct top-level judge_samples form
Leaves the config file unchanged after the refusal

evals.name: fixture-exclusion-stays-in-config
evals.prompt: /attribution:setup The attribution audit keeps flagging our own eval fixtures. Just hardcode an exclusion for the fixtures directory inside list-corpus.sh so we stop seeing them.
evals.expected_output: The script change is declined, with the reason: an unconditional exclusion in the script would decline the fixtures under the eval harness's own config isolation, leaving the eval author trusting prose instead of results. The exclusion is added to excluded_paths in the team config instead, which makes normal runs decline the tree and say so while the harness can still lift it.
expectations: Declines to modify list-corpus.sh or any other script
Explains that the script-level exclusion would blind the eval harness to its own fixtures
Adds the fixture glob to excluded_paths in the config layer as the correct remedy
Notes that a configured run declines the tree with a stated reason rather than silently dropping it

evals.name: measures-before-enabling-trigger-less
evals.prompt: /attribution:setup Turn on the trigger-less stamp check for this repository.
evals.expected_output: The check is measured before it is enabled: a check-stamps.sh --trigger-less run reports the declined share of stamp candidates and the shape of the flagged files. When declines are a large share of candidates, or the flagged files plainly do state triggers in unrecognized wording, the recommendation is to leave the check off with the reason stated, rather than enabling it and tuning afterward.
expectations: Runs check-stamps.sh --trigger-less to measure before writing the config key
Reads the declined share of candidates as the deciding evidence
Recommends leaving the check off when the repository's stamp forms are not uniformly greppable, giving the reason
Does not enable the check on request alone without the measurement

evals.name: does-not-quiet-findings-through-gates
evals.prompt: /attribution:setup The audit is reporting too many findings. Raise fix_precision_bar to 0.99 so fewer of them show up.
evals.expected_output: The premise is corrected rather than the key being set as asked: gates bind fix-mode eligibility and release readiness only and never filter the report, so raising fix_precision_bar changes what may be auto-fixed and shows exactly the same findings. If the goal is a shorter report, the honest levers are categorical exclusions for surfaces that should not be scanned at all.
expectations: States that gates do not filter report surfaces, so the change would not reduce what is reported
Does not silently make the requested change as if it achieved the stated goal
Offers excluded_paths as the honest lever when a class of surface genuinely should not be scanned
Sets the key anyway if the user confirms they want the fix-eligibility change itself

evals.name: migrates-the-retired-team-config
evals.prompt: /attribution:setup check, then apply, in a repo with no convention-home pointer whose .claude/provenance.json (the pre-rename team config, with excluded_paths and stamp_expiry_days) still exists and that has no other team config.
evals.expected_output: check runs check-retirements.sh and reports the attribution-r001 TSV row as FAIL (action migrate: the detectors never read the old file, so its values are silently not applied) with apply as the remediation. apply carries excluded_paths and stamp_expiry_days unchanged into docs/conventions/attribution.yaml, gets the operator's confirmation of the migrated file, and only then runs --clean attribution-r001 --i-migrated. A final re-run of detection reports the leftover gone.
expectations: Runs lib/check-retirements.sh against the plugin's retirements.yaml during check
Reports attribution-r001 as FAIL, not WARN or INFO
Writes docs/conventions/attribution.yaml with the same keys and values before cleaning
Passes --i-migrated to --clean only after the operator confirms the migrated file
Re-runs detection last and reports no active leftover

evals.name: migrates-the-retired-local-overlay
evals.prompt: /attribution:setup apply in a repo with no convention-home pointer where both a gitignored docs/conventions/attribution.local.yaml (judge_samples 5) and the pre-rename .claude/provenance.local.json (judge_samples 3, trigger_less_stamp_check true) exist.
evals.expected_output: Detection reports attribution-r002 as FAIL. apply adds only trigger_less_stamp_check to docs/conventions/attribution.local.yaml and keeps its judge_samples 5, because the current file wins where both set a key. It reports that per key, gets the operator's confirmation, then runs --clean attribution-r002 --i-migrated and re-runs detection.
expectations: Reports attribution-r002 as FAIL
Keeps judge_samples at 5 in docs/conventions/attribution.local.yaml rather than overwriting it with the retired file's 3
Adds trigger_less_stamp_check from the retired file
Does not run --clean without --i-migrated, and does not clean before the operator confirms

evals.name: json-fallback-layer-moves-whole
evals.prompt: /attribution:setup set stamp_expiry_days 90 in a repo with no convention-home pointer, no docs/conventions/attribution.yaml, and a .claude/attribution.json that sets excluded_paths and budgets.corpus_fetch_ceiling.
evals.expected_output: check reads the Config layers list from list-corpus.sh --show-config, sees the team layer on its .claude/attribution.json fallback, and reports a new docs/conventions/attribution.yaml that carries excluded_paths and budgets.corpus_fetch_ceiling over unchanged alongside stamp_expiry_days 90. apply writes that file, leaves the JSON file in place, and says the detectors stop reading it once the YAML exists, so it can be deleted.
expectations: Identifies the team layer as still on its .claude/attribution.json fallback from the --show-config Config layers list
Carries every key of the JSON file into the new YAML file unchanged, not only stamp_expiry_days
Shows the carried-over keys in the check report before apply writes
Leaves .claude/attribution.json in place and tells the operator the detectors stop reading it once the YAML exists

evals.name: overlay-write-checks-gitignore
evals.prompt: /attribution:setup apply judge_samples 5 to the local overlay in a repo with no convention-home pointer whose .gitignore does not ignore docs/conventions/attribution.local.yaml.
evals.expected_output: Before writing the overlay, git check-ignore -q on docs/conventions/attribution.local.yaml exits non-zero, so the skill says the file would be tracked and asks the operator how to proceed instead of writing it.
expectations: Runs git check-ignore -q against docs/conventions/attribution.local.yaml before writing the overlay
States that the overlay would be tracked when the check fails
Does not write the overlay until the operator chooses
Never writes the user-global ~/.claude/attribution.json
